investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the pod never left the pending state, meaning the agent VM was never provisioned.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote-agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes. Two nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported "Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm" — meaning the peer-pod VM quota on those nodes was fully consumed at the time of scheduling. The other 4 nodes did not satisfy the pod's node affinity or node selector constraints and were therefore ineligible. Preemption could not help because no lower-priority victims existed on the two eligible nodes. The pod remained unscheduled for 130–147 seconds across all three checks before the eval timed out, producing an empty evidence object and a full contract-gap on all four required evidence keys (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState). This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity failure localized to the remote-agents swarm scheduling layer in the production-api environment; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource quota exhausted on the 2 eligible nodes: all available peer-pod VM slots were occupied by existing workloads at the time of the eval run, leaving no capacity for new remote-agent pods.

Secondary — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: the 4 non-kata nodes do not match the remote-agent pod's required node selector/affinity, reducing the schedulable node pool to exactly 2 nodes and making the system highly sensitive to any capacity pressure on those nodes.

Tertiary — peer-pod node count too small for the workload: only 2 of 6 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource, meaning a single burst of concurrent remote-agent requests can saturate the entire schedulable pool.

Lower probability — a recent change to node labels, taints, or the pod's affinity spec narrowed the eligible node set, but no suspect changes are present in sourceDiscovery.suspectChanges to support this hypothesis.

If the remote-agent pod spec contains a node selector or affinity rule that was recently changed to exclude the kata-capable nodes, the root cause would shift to a misconfiguration rather than capacity exhaustion.

If a re-run of the eval immediately after this failure succeeds and produces all four required evidence keys (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState), the failure was transient (e.g., a brief burst of concurrent workloads) rather than a sustained capacity shortage.

If only remote-agent-create fails while remote-agent-state or remote-agent-runtime passes in a subsequent run, the failure is not a shared scheduling-layer issue and a check-specific cause should be investigated.

If the Kubernetes event log for the failed pod shows a different rejection reason (e.g., image pull failure, resource quota, or PodSecurityPolicy), the kata.peerpods.io/vm exhaustion diagnosis would need to be revised.

investigation.title: Remote Agents: All Three Checks Failing — Kubernetes Kata Peer-Pods VM Capacity Exhausted on Production Cluster
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-09T01:31–01:36Z with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the cluster's 6 nodes could not schedule the requested kata.peerpods.io/vm pod because 2 nodes had insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the agent pod never became schedulable, the eval runner's createAgent call (run-status-probes.mjs line 1905) never returned an agent, and no evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) was ever written, causing a total contract gap against the expected-output contract defined at check-expectations.json line 264.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes production cluster (6 nodes) exhausted its available kata.peerpods.io/vm resource slots at the time of the eval run. Of the 6 nodes, only 2 support the kata peer-pods VM resource type, and both reported insufficient capacity; the remaining 4 nodes did not satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector constraints. Preemption was also unavailable. As a result, every remote-agent pod submitted during the eval window was stuck Unschedulable for 130–147 seconds before the eval timed out. This is an infrastructure-layer capacity failure localized to the remote-agents Swarm VM scheduling path in the production-api environment. No evidence of a user-traffic or production incident signal is present in the packet; this is an eval-detected capacity constraint.

investigation.title: Remote Agent Eval Failure: Kubernetes kata.peerpods.io/vm Resource Exhaustion Prevents Pod Scheduling
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because the Kubernetes scheduler could not place the required kata peer-pod VM onto any of the 6 available nodes — 2 nodes reported insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. The eval pod remained unscheduled for 147 seconds before the check timed out, producing zero evidence output and failing every required-evidence assertion.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that are eligible by node affinity/selector. With 0 of 6 nodes able to accept the pod and preemption yielding no victims, the scheduler cannot place the remote agent VM pod. This is a cluster-level resource constraint, not an application code defect. The failure is localized to the remote-agents eval in production-api and is an eval infrastructure failure reflecting a real infrastructure constraint; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence to confirm a broader user-facing outage.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the pod never left the pending state, meaning the agent VM was never provisioned.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote-agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes. Two nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported "Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm" — meaning the peer-pod VM quota on those nodes was fully consumed at the time of scheduling. The other 4 nodes did not satisfy the pod's node affinity or node selector constraints and were therefore ineligible. Preemption could not help because no lower-priority victims existed on the two eligible nodes. The pod remained unscheduled for 130–147 seconds across all three checks before the eval timed out, producing an empty evidence object and a full contract-gap on all four required evidence keys (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState). This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity failure localized to the remote-agents swarm scheduling layer in the production-api environment; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:256-258: contract requires vmIdPresent=true and remoteState oneOf [running, idle, ready] — neither assertion could be evaluated because the pod was never scheduled.
possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource quota exhausted on the 2 eligible nodes: all available peer-pod VM slots were occupied by existing workloads at the time of the eval run, leaving no capacity for new remote-agent pods.

Secondary — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: the 4 non-kata nodes do not match the remote-agent pod's required node selector/affinity, reducing the schedulable node pool to exactly 2 nodes and making the system highly sensitive to any capacity pressure on those nodes.

Tertiary — peer-pod node count too small for the workload: only 2 of 6 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource, meaning a single burst of concurrent remote-agent requests can saturate the entire schedulable pool.

Lower probability — a recent change to node labels, taints, or the pod's affinity spec narrowed the eligible node set, but no suspect changes are present in sourceDiscovery.suspectChanges to support this hypothesis.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If kubectl describe nodes shows kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable capacity is available and not fully consumed on the 2 eligible nodes, the root cause is not resource exhaustion and another scheduling constraint must be investigated.

If the remote-agent pod spec contains a node selector or affinity rule that was recently changed to exclude the kata-capable nodes, the root cause would shift to a misconfiguration rather than capacity exhaustion.

If a re-run of the eval immediately after this failure succeeds and produces all four required evidence keys (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState), the failure was transient (e.g., a brief burst of concurrent workloads) rather than a sustained capacity shortage.

If only remote-agent-create fails while remote-agent-state or remote-agent-runtime passes in a subsequent run, the failure is not a shared scheduling-layer issue and a check-specific cause should be investigated.

If the Kubernetes event log for the failed pod shows a different rejection reason (e.g., image pull failure, resource quota, or PodSecurityPolicy), the kata.peerpods.io/vm exhaustion diagnosis would need to be revised.

Consider a concurrent remote-agent creation eval that submits two pods simultaneously to detect capacity exhaustion under minimal load, catching single-slot saturation before it affects production workloads.

investigations.title: Remote Agents: All Three Checks Failing — Kubernetes Kata Peer-Pods VM Capacity Exhausted on Production Cluster
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-09T01:31–01:36Z with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the cluster's 6 nodes could not schedule the requested kata.peerpods.io/vm pod because 2 nodes had insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the agent pod never became schedulable, the eval runner's createAgent call (run-status-probes.mjs line 1905) never returned an agent, and no evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) was ever written, causing a total contract gap against the expected-output contract defined at check-expectations.json line 264.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes production cluster (6 nodes) exhausted its available kata.peerpods.io/vm resource slots at the time of the eval run. Of the 6 nodes, only 2 support the kata peer-pods VM resource type, and both reported insufficient capacity; the remaining 4 nodes did not satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector constraints. Preemption was also unavailable. As a result, every remote-agent pod submitted during the eval window was stuck Unschedulable for 130–147 seconds before the eval timed out. This is an infrastructure-layer capacity failure localized to the remote-agents Swarm VM scheduling path in the production-api environment. No evidence of a user-traffic or production incident signal is present in the packet; this is an eval-detected capacity constraint.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Eval Failure: Kubernetes kata.peerpods.io/vm Resource Exhaustion Prevents Pod Scheduling
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because the Kubernetes scheduler could not place the required kata peer-pod VM onto any of the 6 available nodes — 2 nodes reported insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. The eval pod remained unscheduled for 147 seconds before the check timed out, producing zero evidence output and failing every required-evidence assertion.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that are eligible by node affinity/selector. With 0 of 6 nodes able to accept the pod and preemption yielding no victims, the scheduler cannot place the remote agent VM pod. This is a cluster-level resource constraint, not an application code defect. The failure is localized to the remote-agents eval in production-api and is an eval infrastructure failure reflecting a real infrastructure constraint; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence to confirm a broader user-facing outage.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1910-1918: the runner calls createAgent(args, track, 'remote', null, orgId) at line 1918, which must provision a remote VM pod — this is the step that blocks on scheduling
possibleCauses: Primary: kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource is fully consumed on the 2 affinity-eligible nodes in the production-api cluster, leaving no schedulable capacity for new remote agent pods.

Secondary: The 4 remaining nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity or node selector rules (e.g., a label such as kata-containers=true or a specific node pool label is absent), reducing the effective scheduling domain to only 2 nodes, both of which are already at capacity.

Tertiary: A prior eval run or a concurrent workload left one or more remote agent pods running and not cleaned up, consuming the finite kata.peerpods.io/vm slots on the eligible nodes. The withCleanup wrapper in run-status-probes.mjs (line 1916) is intended to release resources, but if a previous run crashed before cleanup, leaked pods could hold the resource.

Lower probability: The cluster's kata peer-pods provider (e.g., cloud VM quota or peer-pod controller capacity) has an upstream limit that is currently exhausted, preventing the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource from being replenished even if pods are deleted.

reproductionSteps.details: Use the same environment variables as the scheduled observability workflow to reproduce the scheduling failure.

reproductionSteps.details: Identify which nodes advertise the resource, how much is allocatable, and how much is currently requested.

reproductionSteps.details: Identify any stuck, pending, or running pods holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots that should have been cleaned up.

affectedAreas.label: Remote Agents feature — all three eval checks
affectedAreas.reason: All three checks registered under the remote-agents feature (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed with the same Unschedulable cause, implicating the entire remote agent VM provisioning path.
affectedAreas.details: features.json lines 183-185 register all three checks; degradedAfterFailures=1 and outageAfterFailures=2 mean two required-check failures (remote-agent-create and remote-agent-state) already satisfy the outage threshold for this feature.

affectedAreas.label: Kubernetes kata peer-pods scheduling layer (production-api cluster)
affectedAreas.reason: The scheduler message 'Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm' on 2/6 nodes and node affinity mismatch on 4/6 nodes is the direct blocking condition. This is a cluster infrastructure area, not application code.
affectedAreas.details: 0/6 nodes available; preemption found no victims, indicating no lower-priority pods are holding the resource that could be evicted.

affectedAreas.label: Remote agent VM pod provisioning — createAgent('remote') call path
affectedAreas.reason: The runner at line 1918 calls createAgent(args, track, 'remote', null, orgId), which triggers the pod creation that fails to schedule. No evidence was collected because the pod never started.
affectedAreas.details: run-status-probes.mjs lines 1913-1918 show the eval runner branch and the createAgent call.

affectedAreas.label: Expected-output contract for remote-agent-runtime
affectedAreas.reason: All 5 required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) and the message assertion ('hello from aura') were unmet because the agent pod never reached a running state.
affectedAreas.details: check-expectations.json lines 266-270 define the contract; expected-output.missing-required-evidence confirms all 5 fields absent.

recommendedNextActions: Immediately check kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable vs. requested capacity on the 2 eligible nodes to determine if the resource is fully consumed and by which pods.

Audit running pods in the remote-agents namespace for any leaked eval pods that were not cleaned up by the withCleanup wrapper in run-status-probes.mjs (line 1916); terminate any stuck or orphaned pods to free kata.peerpods.io/vm slots.

Investigate why only 2 of 6 nodes match the remote agent pod's node affinity/selector — confirm whether the 4 non-matching nodes are intentionally excluded (e.g., wrong node pool) or whether a node label was removed or is missing.

If resource exhaustion is confirmed and not caused by leaked pods, evaluate whether the kata peer-pods node pool needs additional nodes or whether the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource limit per node needs to be increased to support concurrent eval runs.
Review the withCleanup mechanism in infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs to ensure it handles crash/timeout scenarios and does not leave pods running when the eval runner exits abnormally.

Monitor whether the remote-agent-create and remote-agent-state checks (both marked required=true in features.json lines 183-184) continue to fail, as two required-check failures satisfy the outageAfterFailures=2 threshold for the remote-agents feature.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: Inspect kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity on all cluster nodes
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Directly confirms whether the resource is exhausted on the 2 eligible nodes and whether the 4 non-eligible nodes lack the required node labels, proving or disproving the scheduling exhaustion hypothesis.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: List pods currently holding kata.peerpods.io/vm resources to detect leaked eval pods
recommendedVerifierProbes.command: kubectl get pods --all-namespaces -o json | jq '.items[] | select(.spec.containers[].resources.requests["kata.peerpods.io/vm"] != null) | {name: .metadata.name, namespace: .metadata.namespace, phase: .status.phase}'
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Identifies whether prior eval runs left pods running that are consuming the finite kata.peerpods.io/vm slots, which would explain why new pods cannot be scheduled.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: Re-run the failed expected-output contract after verifying cluster capacity
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Confirms whether the scheduling failure is still present or has self-resolved, and whether the eval can now collect the required evidence (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message).

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: Check Kubernetes events for the unscheduled pod to get the exact resource request and node selector
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Surfaces the exact pod name, namespace, resource request quantity, and node selector that caused the FailedScheduling event, providing precise evidence for the scheduling constraint.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: Verify node labels on all 6 nodes to confirm which 2 are kata-eligible
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Confirms whether the 4 nodes that failed affinity/selector matching are missing expected labels (e.g., kata-containers=true or equivalent), distinguishing a node pool misconfiguration from pure resource exhaustion.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If kubectl describe nodes showed kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable capacity available on the eligible nodes at the time of the failure, the scheduling exhaustion hypothesis would be weakened and a different cause (e.g., a misconfigured resource request or a broken kata runtime) would need to be investigated.

If the 4 nodes that failed node affinity/selector matching were actually eligible (i.e., the node labels are correct and present), then the affinity rules on the pod spec may have been changed incorrectly, shifting the root cause to a pod spec misconfiguration rather than resource exhaustion.
If a subsequent eval run immediately after this failure succeeded without any cluster changes, it would suggest a transient scheduling race rather than sustained resource exhaustion.

If leaked pods from prior eval runs were not found consuming kata.peerpods.io/vm slots, the exhaustion would be attributable to non-eval workloads or a reduced node pool, not to cleanup failures in the eval runner.
If the local-agent-runtime or local-agent-create checks were also failing at the same time, it would suggest a broader API or authentication failure rather than a kata-specific scheduling problem.
followUpEvals: Add a pre-flight eval check that queries kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable vs. requested capacity across all eligible nodes before attempting remote agent creation, and fails fast with a descriptive capacity message rather than waiting for a scheduling timeout.
Add an eval that detects and reports leaked remote agent pods (pods in a non-terminal state that were created by prior eval runs and not cleaned up), alerting before resource exhaustion occurs.

Add a node-pool health eval that verifies the expected number of kata-eligible nodes (matching the required node affinity/selector) are Ready and advertising kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity above a minimum threshold.

Consider a canary eval that attempts a minimal remote agent pod scheduling dry-run (using kubectl --dry-run=server) without actually starting the agent, to detect scheduling failures earlier and with lower resource cost.
